original_interpretation: US-HQ chip firms' 2025 sales were US$425bn, 53.4% of world sales, highest US share since 1984 (SIA estimate).
evidence_found: "The U.S. industry reached sales of $425 billion in 2025, representing 53.4% of total global sales and the highest U.S. market share since 1984." Chart 'GLOBAL MARKET SHARE BY COMPANY HQ, 2025', 'Source: WSTS, Gartner, Omdia, and SIA estimates' (SIA 2026 SOTI, PDF p.7)
notes: Opened the SIA PDF. claim_type estimate fits: it is an SIA estimate that attributes sales by company HQ.

original_interpretation: SIA's 2026 SOTI gives 2025 global sales of US$795.6bn, replacing the US$791.7bn SIA first announced in Feb 2026.
evidence_found: "Global semiconductor sales reached $795.6 billion in 2025, far exceeding initial forecasts and setting a record for the industry." (SIA 2026 SOTI, p.6). SIA 6 Feb 2026: "global semiconductor sales hit $791.7 billion in 2025, an increase of 25.6%".
notes: Both figures match their sources. SIA does not use the word 'replacing'; the US$795.6bn is the later (WSTS-finalised) vintage, which matches the WSTS Q4 and Spring 2026 releases.

original_interpretation: SIA 2026 SOTI: 2025 logic US$299.5bn (+38.8%), memory US$230.0bn (+39.0%), replacing Feb 2026 US$301.9bn / US$223.1bn.
evidence_found: "Sales of logic chips totaled $299.5 billion in 2025, increasing by 38.8% year-on-year ... Memory products were second in sales at $230.0 billion in 2025, a 39.0% sales increase over 2024." (SIA 2026 SOTI p.6). SIA Feb 2026: "logic products increased by 39.9%, totaling $301.9 billion ... Memory ... a total of $223.1 billion."
notes: Also matches the WSTS Spring 2026 table (Logic 299,547; Memory 230,042 US$M).

original_interpretation: Gartner's latest 2025 worldwide semiconductor revenue figure is US$809.0bn (Aug 2026), up from US$793.4bn (Jan) and US$805.3bn (Apr).
evidence_found: Aug 2026: "increasing 92% from 2025 revenue of $809 billion"; Table 1 "Total Market | 809.0" (Source: Gartner (August 2026)). Apr 2026 Table 1: "Total Market | 805.3". Jan 2026 Table 1: "Total Market | 793,449" ($M, preliminary).
notes: All three numbers match. A web search found no Gartner release newer than 24 Aug 2026 that changes the 2025 figure (a Gartner 2Q26 forecast document of 26 Jun 2026 is older). The sources are Gartner newsroom pages on the gcom.pdo.aws.gartner.com host, with the same paths as gartner.com/en/newsroom.

original_interpretation: Arm's May 2026 shareholder letter (FYE26) says over 350bn Arm-based chips have shipped cumulatively.
evidence_found: "With over 350 billion chips shipped and over 22 million developers, the Arm compute platform is the most comprehensive in history" (Exhibit 99.2 Shareholder Letter, Form 6-K filed 2026-05-06; read in the SEC EDGAR copy exhibit992fye26q431-marx26.htm, accession 0001973239-26-000062)
notes: curl got a 403 from investors.arm.com and web_extract returned only part of the letter, so I checked the text in the identical EDGAR exhibit of the same filing. The wording is the same, so I added no source. Currency: the Q1 FYE27 6-K Exhibit 99.2 (29 Jul 2026) and the Arm newsroom post do not update the cumulative chip count. reported_claim is the right type.

original_interpretation: Japan announced restrictions on HF, fluorinated polyimides and photoresists to Korea on 1 Jul 2019; Cabinet approved Group A removal 2 Aug 2019; effective 28 Aug 2019.
evidence_found: USITC ID-062 p.4: "On July 1, 2019, Japan announced that it would restrict exports of certain key semiconductor manufacturing materials to Korea. These materials—hydrogen fluoride, fluorinated polyimides, and photoresist/resist". EY: "removed Korea from its Group A list (formerly known as 'white country' list) on 2 August 2019 (Korea was officially removed from the list on 28 August)". CISTEC (2 Aug 2019): "on August 2, Cabinet approved partial amendments to the export trade control order which removes ROK from 'White Countries'..., which will be effective on August 28."
notes: The CISTEC note was published the same day as the Cabinet decision. It confirms the 28 Aug effective date, which the claim had rested on EY (tier 3) for. USITC fn 20 also cites METI's 2 Aug 2019 release on the Cabinet amendment.

original_interpretation: USITC 2019 paper cites an SIA estimate: as of 2017 the National IC Fund had ~US$21bn and local IC funds >US$80bn, toward a combined US$150bn goal.
evidence_found: "The SIA estimated that, as of 2017, while the National IC Fund had secured roughly $21 billion in funding, provincial and municipal IC-related funds have raised over $80 billion and are well on their way to reaching the goal of $150 billion.71" fn 71: "Adapted from USTR, Section 301 Report, March 22, 2017 [sic], 92 and 94." (VerWey, JICE July 2019, p.13)
correction: The source does not call the US$150bn goal 'combined'. Grammatically it is the goal the provincial/municipal funds are 'well on their way to reaching'. Drop 'combined' or say 'a US$150bn goal'.
notes: The US$21bn, >US$80bn and SIA attribution are verbatim. Footnote 71 dates the USTR report 'March 22, 2017', which looks like a typo for 2018 (fn 63-65 give 2018). The same paper (p.12) also says the Fund was 'Endowed with $150 billion in funds from the central and provincial governments', so what the $150bn refers to is unclear in the source.

original_interpretation: AMD completed Asset Smart with ATIC and Mubadala in early 2009, creating GLOBALFOUNDRIES, consolidated from 2 Mar 2009.
evidence_found: "AMD completed its Asset Smart transaction with the Advanced Technology Investment Company (ATIC) and Mubadala Development Company of Abu Dhabi, creating GLOBALFOUNDRIES"; "For financial reporting purposes, AMD consolidates the operating results of GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. in its results as of March 2, 2009" (AMD Q1 2009 release, Ex. 99.1, 21 Apr 2009, p.1)
notes: The release is AMD's own earnings release filed as an 8-K exhibit, so company_filing is accurate.

original_interpretation: 15 U.S.C. 4651(2) definition of CHIPS 'covered entity'.
evidence_found: "(2) The term \"covered entity\" means a nonprofit entity, a private entity, a consortium of private entities, or a consortium of nonprofit, public, and private entities with a demonstrated ability to substantially finance, construct, expand, or modernize a facility relating to fabrication, assembly, testing, advanced packaging, production, or research and development of semiconductors, materials used to manufacture semiconductors, or semiconductor manufacturing equipment." (uscode.house.gov, 'laws in effect on September 12, 2026'; same text at LII)
notes: The definition is current in the OLRC prelim edition (in effect 12 Sep 2026). On a later retry uscode.house.gov showed 'Under Maintenance', but the earlier extract this run returned the full text. LII matches word for word.

original_interpretation: ITA said overseas packaging/assembly and transshipments skew semiconductor trade data, so it used WSTS regional market data.
evidence_found: "It was difficult in the case of semiconductors, however, due to overseas packaging and final assembly of semiconductors and transshipments skewing the import and export data." ... "This has improved the methodology for semiconductors, as the WSTS data is used in this year's calculation." (2016 ITA Top Markets Report, Executive Summary, p.3, Methodology)
notes: The original legacy.trade.gov URL (SRC-0026) failed this run (SSL certificate error, then 404), so I verified against the Wayback capture SRC-0859. The data is from 2016 and historical.

original_interpretation: TrendForce: top-10 foundry revenue nearly US$46.3bn in 4Q25 (incl. Samsung Foundry excl. System LSI); TSMC 70.4% share.
evidence_found: "pushed the combined revenue of the world's top ten foundries up 2.6% QoQ to nearly US$46.3 billion in 4Q25"; "quarterly revenue 2% QoQ to $33.7 billion, which allowed TSMC to maintain its leading position with a 70.4% market share"; "Samsung Foundry (excluding System LSI) recorded 6.7% QoQ revenue growth" (TrendForce press release, 12 Mar 2026)
notes: This is a public TrendForce press release, so estimate / research_firm is right. TrendForce has not yet published a 1Q26 ranking that would supersede the 4Q25 figures; the claim is clearly dated to 4Q25 in any case.

original_interpretation: WSTS final 2025 results (6 Mar 2026): global sales US$795.6bn, +26.2%.
evidence_found: "The World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) organization released full-year 2025 semiconductor market results, incorporating finalized fourth-quarter data. Global semiconductor sales reached USD 795.6 billion in 2025, representing an increase of 26.2 percent year-over-year" (WSTS release, 6 Mar 2026, p.1); Spring 2026 table "Total World - $M 795,640 ... 26.2"

original_interpretation: EPRS (May 2026) reports the ECA warned the 20% 2030 share target was unlikely, citing a Commission forecast of 11.7%.
evidence_found: "Finally, the ECA warned that the 20 % global market share target by 2030 was unlikely to be achieved, and stressed that the Commission's own forecast projects only 11.7 % by 2030." (EPRS briefing PE 785.742, 'Published: May 2026', p.4)
notes: The claim correctly presents this as second-hand. The 11.7% is a forecast, not an actual. I did not open the ECA special report itself.

original_interpretation: Reagan announced 100% duties on up to US$300m of Japanese exports on 27 Mar 1987 and proclaimed the Section 301 tariff increases effective 17 Apr 1987.
evidence_found: "On March 27, 1987, I announced my intention to raise customs duties to a level of 100 percent ad valorem on as much as $300 million in Japanese exports to the United States"; "The tariff increases I am proclaiming shall be effective with respect to the covered products of Japan which are entered on and after April 17, 1987." (Memorandum, 17 Apr 1987)
notes: The source says the 27 Mar announcement was of an 'intention' to raise duties. The claim's 'announced ... duties' is a fair reading.

original_interpretation: WSTS Spring 2026 puts 2025 sales at US$795.6bn (+26.2%), revising SIA's Feb 2026 US$791.7bn (+25.6%).
evidence_found: WSTS Spring 2026 table (2 Jun 2026): "Total World - $M 795,640 1,511,248 1,913,683 26.2 89.9 26.6" (2025 column first). SIA 6 Feb 2026: "global semiconductor sales hit $791.7 billion in 2025, an increase of 25.6% compared to the 2024 total of $630.5 billion."
notes: The final 2025 figure first appeared in the WSTS Q4 release of 6 Mar 2026 (SRC-0862); the Spring release repeats it.

original_interpretation: WSTS Spring 2026 puts 2025 memory sales at US$230.0bn (+39.0%), revising SIA's Feb 2026 US$223.1bn (+34.8%).
evidence_found: WSTS Spring 2026 table: "Memory 230,042 803,941 1,062,085 39.0 249.5 32.1". SIA 6 Feb 2026: "Memory products were second in terms of sales, increasing by 34.8% in 2024 to a total of $223.1 billion."
notes: The SIA release says 'in 2024', which is SIA's typo for 2025. The claim marks it [sic] in its evidence.

original_interpretation: SIA 2026 SOTI: US companies spent US$76.8bn on R&D in 2025, +10.3% from US$69.6bn in 2024.
evidence_found: "American semiconductor companies spent $76.8 billion on R&D in 2025, up from $69.6 billion in 2024 and representing a 10.3% increase in R&D spend." Chart 'R&D EXPENDITURES, U.S.-HEADQUARTERED COMPANIES, 2001-2025', "Source: SIA, 2026 Factbook" (SIA 2026 SOTI p.13)
notes: The text matches. The 'company 10-K/10-Q filings' detail in metric.methodology is not in this document, whose chart only cites 'SIA, 2026 Factbook'. Treat that detail as unverified here. Also, 76.8/69.6 = +10.3%, which is consistent. 'fact' is generous for an SIA compilation; 'estimate' would also be defensible.

original_interpretation: Synopsys: most EDA licences are network licences; EDA sold via TSLs of generally 2-3 years; time-based subscription and perpetual+support arrangements refer to S&A software.
evidence_found: Item 1: "The majority of licenses to our EDA products and Ansys semiconductor products are network licenses"; "Our S&A software solutions are offered as subscription solutions and also as perpetual licenses. Software subscription arrangements include bundles of time-based software licenses with support services". MD&A critical accounting estimates: "EDA products and services are typically sold through Technology Subscription License (TSL) arrangements ... The duration of our TSL contracts is generally two to three years" (Synopsys 10-K FY ended 31 Oct 2025)
notes: Read the EDGAR primary document directly. S&A = 'simulation and analysis' (Item 1). The network-licence sentence also covers 'Ansys semiconductor products', not only EDA.

original_interpretation: Intel's 21 Jan 2022 release announced an initial investment of >US$20bn for two leading-edge fabs in Licking County, Ohio.
evidence_found: "LICKING COUNTY, Ohio--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Intel today announced plans for an initial investment of more than $20 billion in the construction of two new leading-edge chip factories in Ohio."; "total investment in the site could grow to as much as $100 billion over the next decade" (Intel press release PDF, 21 Jan 2022, p.1)
notes: reported_claim is the right type: it is a company announcement of planned investment, not spending that has happened.

original_interpretation: TSMC FY2025 20-F: TSMC owned ~72.6% of JASM as of 28 Feb 2026, with Sony, DENSO and Toyota holding minority stakes.
evidence_found: "In January 2022, Sony ... acquired a less than 20% equity interest in JASM. In April 2022, DENSO ... acquired a more than 10% minority equity interest in JASM. ... By way of such investment, Toyota also took a minority stake in JASM. As of February 28, 2026, we owned approximately 72.6% of the equity interest in JASM." (Form 20-F FY2025, Item 4, pp.25-26)
notes: Read the EDGAR primary document directly.

original_interpretation: TSMC FY2025 20-F: machinery and equipment depreciated over 5 years, buildings over 10-20 years, straight-line.
evidence_found: "it is computed using the straight-line method mainly over the following estimated useful lives: land improvements - 10 to 20 years; buildings (assets used by the Company and assets subject to operating leases) - 10 to 20 years; machinery and equipment (...) - 5 years; and office equipment - 5 years." (Form 20-F FY2025, notes to consolidated financial statements, property, plant and equipment)

original_interpretation: TSMC's first US fab is TSMC Washington (ex-WaferTech, Fab 11) in Washington State: a JV set up in 1996, commercial production from Oct 1998, 100% owned as of 28 Feb 2026.
evidence_found: "In 1996, we entered into a joint venture called WaferTech (of which the manufacturing entity is Fab 11) with several U.S.-based investors ... Initial trial production at WaferTech commenced in July 1998 and commercial production commenced in October 1998. In December 2023, WaferTech was renamed as TSMC Washington. As of February 28, 2026, we owned 100% of the equity interest in TSMC Washington."; land "in the State of Washington in the United States" (Form 20-F FY2025, Item 4)

original_interpretation: TWSE says MOPS was set up 1 Aug 2002 under FSC SFB guidance by TWSE, TPEx and others; revamped 2010; optimized MOPS launched 21 Oct 2024.
evidence_found: "公開資訊觀測站係經行政院金融監督管理委員會證券期貨局指導，由臺灣證券交易所股份有限公司、財團法人中華民國證券櫃檯買賣中心等相關單位共同合作，於民國91年8月1日建立之網站"; "歷經99年改版上線以來"; "優化公開資訊觀測站於113年10月21日正式對外服務" (TWSE 文刊中心, 113/11/28)
notes: The ROC-year conversions (91=2002, 99=2010, 113=2024) are correct. reported_claim fits: the exchange is describing its own platform.

original_interpretation: TPEx moved Grand Process Technology (3131) from Other Electronic to Semiconductor from 1 Jun 2026; Gudeng (3680) was not among the 13 reclassified.
evidence_found: CNA 2026-05-19: "櫃買中心今天公告，川寶、泰茂、全域、弘塑、斐成、台聯電訊、欣厚、光譜電工、廣運、華電聯網、中湛、友鋮、智通科創等13家上櫃公司，將調整產業類別，自今年6月1日起實施"; "全域與弘塑由其他電子業分別調整為居家生活、半導體業". MOPS Aug 2026, 產業別：半導體業: "3131 弘塑 681,351"
notes: Gudeng (3680 家登) is not in CNA's list. It already appears in the same MOPS 半導體業 table ("3680 家登 839,771"), so it was already in the Semiconductor category. 'Semiconductor equipment maker' is not in either source. The company describes itself as a semiconductor wet-processing equipment maker (gptc.com.tw/en/about, not added as a source).

original_interpretation: CSRC Order 226 (in force 1 Jul 2025): periodic reports are the annual report (within 4 months of FYE) and interim report (within 2 months of H1 end).
evidence_found: "第十二条 上市公司应当披露的定期报告包括年度报告、中期报告。" "第十三条 年度报告应当在每个会计年度结束之日起四个月内，中期报告应当在每个会计年度的上半年结束之日起两个月内，编制完成并披露。" "第六十七条 本办法自2025年7月1日起施行。2021年3月18日发布的《上市公司信息披露管理办法》（证监会令第182号）同时废止。" (Order 226 text, CSRC attachment 附件1)
notes: The MOJ copy (SRC-0874) would not open this run (extractor error, redirect loop, browser timeout). I verified against the original attachment linked from the CSRC Order 226 page (SRC-0875), csrc.gov.cn/.../7547359/files/附件1：上市公司信息披露管理办法.pdf, which has the same wording. Art. 67 shows the Order repealed CSRC Order 182 (2021), not the 2007 Measures directly.

original_interpretation: CSRC Order 226 requires Chinese-language disclosure (Chinese prevails) and publication on the exchange website and CSRC-qualified media.
evidence_found: "第十条 信息披露文件应当采用中文文本。同时采用外文文本的，信息披露义务人应当保证两种文本的内容一致。两种文本发生歧义时，以中文文本为准。" "第八条 依法披露的信息，应当在证券交易所的网站和符合中国证监会规定条件的媒体发布，同时将其置备于上市公司住所、证券交易所，供社会公众查阅。" (Order 226 text, CSRC attachment 附件1)
notes: Checked against the CSRC original attachment, because the MOJ copy (SRC-0874) would not open this run.

original_interpretation: TWSE Key Points (2025.06.09): initial-listing industry is set by >50% of operating income in each of the two latest FYs (or >=80% in the latest FY); TWSE adjusts categories every year.
evidence_found: Point 3: "發行公司初次申請股票上市時，其最近二個會計年度之財務報告，均符合下列各款情形之一者...（一）公司有所營任何一項業務之營業收入占其全部營業收入之比率超過百分之五十以上者，以該項業務為其上市產業類別"; "其最近一個會計年度之財務報告...超過百分之八十以上者"; Point 5: "本公司每年定期調整各上市公司之產業類別" (Chinese text 114.06.09)
notes: The English translation says "on a biyearly basis" and "fifty percent (50%) or more", and adds: "In case of any discrepancy between the Chinese version ... and this English translation, the Chinese version shall prevail." The Chinese text supports 'every year'. '超過百分之五十以上' is loosely worded; the English renders it '50% or more'.

original_interpretation: TrendForce News (3 Nov 2025) attributes to TrendForce both the shift from quarterly to monthly DRAM quotes and Samsung largely halting contract offers.
evidence_found: "The pricing cycle has also shifted from quarterly frameworks to monthly quotes, according to TrendForce." "TrendForce adds that currently, Samsung has largely halted contract offers, while other suppliers have adopted a wait-and-see stance, fueling a bidding atmosphere that continues to drive DRAM prices sharply higher." (TrendForce News, 3 Nov 2025)
notes: Both statements carry an explicit TrendForce attribution in the article. The headline uses 'Reportedly', and the article also cites Commercial Times and TechNews.

original_interpretation: June 2009: Elpida to sell JPY30bn of securities to the government-backed DBJ as part of a JPY160bn package including public funds.
evidence_found: "Japanese chip-maker Elpida was thrown a 160 billion yen (US$1.7 billion) financial lifeline Tuesday, including public funds"; "will sell securities worth 30 billion yen to the government-backed Development Bank of Japan, which will also extend it a loan of 10 billion yen." (IndustryWeek/AFP, 30 Jun 2009)
notes: The source says Elpida 'will sell', as announced in the trade ministry's statement, which matches 'agreed to sell'. The JPY160bn breaks down as 30 + 10 (DBJ loan) + 20 (Taiwan Memory) + 100 (private-bank loans). This is a single tier-2 press report; I did not open the METI statement.

original_interpretation: Regulation (EU) 2026/1386 of 17 Jun 2026 repeals 2019/452; published in the OJ 26 Jun 2026.
evidence_found: EUR-Lex: "OJ L, 2026/1386, 26.6.2026"; "REGULATION (EU) 2026/1386 ... of 17 June 2026 on the screening of foreign investments in the Union and repealing Regulation (EU) 2019/452"; "Done at Strasbourg, 17 June 2026." HK TID: "Regulation (EU) 2026/1386 was published on 26 June 2026"
notes: Read the full EUR-Lex text in the browser. EUR-Lex shows status 'In force'.

original_interpretation: Reg. 2026/1386 entered into force 16 Jul 2026, applies from 17 Jan 2028, with certain articles applying from 16 Jul 2026.
evidence_found: EUR-Lex Article 31: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union. It shall apply from 17 January 2028. However, Article 3(2), Article 15(2), Article 18(1) to (6), Article 18(9) to (12), and Articles 27, 28 and 29 shall apply from 16 July 2026." HK TID para 4: "The Regulation will enter into force on 16 July 2026 and apply from 17 January 2028"
notes: The twentieth day after publication on 26 Jun 2026 is 16 Jul 2026, which matches.

original_interpretation: Reg. 2026/1386 sets a common minimum sectoral scope for mandatory prior authorisation in all member states that includes semiconductors.
evidence_found: EUR-Lex Art. 4(15): "Each Member State shall ensure that its screening mechanism imposes a prior authorisation requirement for foreign investments where the Union target established in its territory: ... (c) produces, conducts research in or develops semiconductor or quantum technologies referred to in Annex I to this Regulation"; Annex I: "TECHNOLOGY AREAS RELEVANT FOR THE COMMON MINIMUM SCOPE PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 4(15) 1. Semiconductor technologies". HK TID para 2 says the same.
notes: Confirmed in the legal text, which is stronger than the HK circular the claim cites. The scope covers Union targets producing, researching or developing the semiconductor technologies listed in Annex I, not every investment in the sector. Greenfield investments are excluded from the prior-authorisation requirement (recital 28).

original_interpretation: Rapidus says it completed a JPY267.6bn round on 27 Feb 2026: JPY100bn from IPA and JPY167.6bn from 32 private companies.
evidence_found: "Rapidus Corporation today announced that it has completed a funding round totaling 267.6 billion yen (equivalent to $1.7 billion USD) from the Japan government and private sector companies. A total of 100 billion yen was invested from the Information-Technology Promotion Agency (IPA)"; "private-sector funding, totaling 167.6 billion yen from 32 companies" (Rapidus news, 27 Feb 2026)
notes: reported_claim is the right type. The 'private' group includes Development Bank of Japan, which the release itself calls a 'government-affiliated financial institution'. Stated capital incl. legal capital surplus after this round: JPY274.95bn.

original_interpretation: Rapidus says it completed an additional JPY150bn IPA round on 5 Jun 2026, bringing stated capital plus legal capital surplus to JPY424.95bn.
evidence_found: "completed an additional funding round of 150 billion yen (equivalent to $943 million USD) from the Information-Technology Promotion Agency (IPA)"; "As a result of this latest capital increase by the IPA, Rapidus funding now totals 424.95 billion yen."; "Capital (as of June 5, 2026): 424.95 billion yen (including legal capital surplus)" (Rapidus news, 5 Jun 2026)
notes: 274.95 + 150 = 424.95, which is consistent.

original_interpretation: Korea's Cabinet approved the Semiconductor Special Act enforcement decree on 4 Aug 2026; the Act and decree took effect 11 Aug 2026.
evidence_found: MOTIR (4 Aug 2026): "「반도체산업 경쟁력 강화 및 지원에 관한 특별법 시행령」 제정안이 8.4.(화) 국무회의에서 의결되었다"; "「반도체특별법」과 이번 시행령 제정안은 8.11(화)부터 본격 시행될 예정이다". Korea Herald (4 Aug): "enforcement rules approved by the Cabinet on Tuesday"; "The decree ... will take effect Aug. 11". MLex public summary: "allowing both the act and the decree to take effect simultaneously on Aug. 11 as scheduled"
notes: I added the ministry's own release (tier 1), which the claim noted it had not read. It gives the 4 Aug Cabinet approval and the 11 Aug start for both the Act and the decree, and says the Act was enacted on 2.10 (10 Feb 2026). ETNews English (12 Aug 2026) confirms the Act 'took effect on Aug. 11' (seen, not added). MLex is paywalled; only its summary was visible.

original_interpretation: DoC announced 29 Jul 2026 letters of intent with 7 companies for US$874m of CHIPS R&D incentives, with a minority non-controlling equity stake in each as a condition.
evidence_found: "The Department of Commerce today announced the signing of 7 letters of intent to provide $874 million in federal incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act."; "The Department will receive a minority, non-controlling equity stake in each company as a condition for receiving the funds to enhance the return for the U.S. taxpayer." (NIST news, 'Released July 29, 2026')
notes: These are letters of intent, not final awards: 'there will be further diligence and approval by the Department before final awards are made'. The 'up to' amounts per company add up to US$874m (300+245+140+75+50+34+30).
